text:
PKIX-lwr9.1 empirical finding (2026-05-11): of the 25 fixtures imported across the five failure-mode buckets, pkix-path-builder + pkix-path PASSES 23 of 25 end-to-end. Only tc60 is a genuine path-builder bug (corpus-expected SUCCESS, builds a chain that fails signature verification at index 3 of a depth-6 chain). tc41 is corpus-expected FAILURE and correctly rejected.

Root cause of the 47-case figure in baseline-limbo.json: pkix-difftest/src/corpus/limbo.rs::build_item builds positional chains [peer, ..intermediates, anchor] and feeds them DIRECTLY to pkix_path::validate_path, BYPASSING pkix-path-builder entirely. PKIX-yn3e (AKI-based candidate selection, 2026-05-08) already shipped before the limbo baseline was generated, but the limbo harness never invokes the builder.

Recommendation: before working PKIX-lwr9.2/.3/.4, verify whether the path-builder is actually broken on the wider 47-case set, or whether the issue is at the limbo-harness layer (which never runs the builder). Two possible scopes:

(a) Update pkix-difftest/src/corpus/limbo.rs to route the CertPath bundle through pkix_path_builder::build_path before classification — mirrors PKIX-t0w4's PKITS harness change. Likely flips most of the 47 StricterThanWild cases to Agreement on rerun, leaving only the real path-builder bugs (probably tc60-shaped). The remaining "real" failures become the actual PKIX-lwr9.2/.3/.4 scope.

(b) Accept that the limbo pathbuilding suite tests consumer-supplied chain ordering, document the divergence, and close PKIX-lwr9 as not-applicable to pkix-path-builder.

Option (a) is more aligned with the bead title. Fixtures + characterization harness landed at pkix-path-builder/tests/bettertls.rs with baseline-pkix-path.json (23/25 passing today). Persistent memory key: pkix-lwr9-1-empirical-finding-2026-05-11.
